tasks.title: Phase 0 feasibility lab and go/no-go decision
tasks.body: Deliverable: the Phase 0 go/no-go measurements that gated the .strm/NFO architecture. Evidence: docs/phase-0-lab.md, docs/phase-0-results.md, lab/, commits `5283201` (planning + policy core) and `ffe3a85` (executable conformance).

children.title: Measure .strm extraction/probing at scan time (A1)
children.body: Measured 0 bytes pulled from a remote .strm during scan, full metadata refresh, trickplay/chapter/keyframe tasks. docs/phase-0-results.md section 2.

children.title: Test local-plus-remote version grouping (A2)
children.body: Confirmed two cards by default; POST /Videos/MergeVersions validated as mitigation. docs/phase-0-results.md section 3.

children.title: Test music grouping and duplication (A3)
children.body: Confirmed duplicate artists/albums/tracks; NFO did not repair. Music cut from v1. docs/phase-0-results.md section 5.

children.title: Synthetic catalog scale test (A5)
children.body: 50,001-item run: 2.94h at 4.72 items/s, 187 MB DB (~3.7 KB/item). docs/phase-0-results.md section 4.

children.title: Token and path leakage test (B6)
children.body: Non-admin could read peer origin URL and stream 2 MB through /Videos/{id}/stream. docs/phase-0-results.md section 6.

tasks.title: Independent plan review and architecture corrections
tasks.body: Deliverable: independent review of the planning phase, with findings resolved, superseded, or reopened as code landed. Evidence: docs/plan-review.md (r4), docs/follow-up-decisions.md.

tasks.title: Policy core: publication, opt-out, blocks, invitations
tasks.body: Deliverable: internal/policy and internal/settings model private-by-default publication, per-library destination opt-out, symmetric pairwise blocks, and invitations, consulting the replicated roster. Evidence: internal/policy/, internal/settings/, README background; criteria C-BL-1..5, C-PO-1..5.

tasks.title: Node identity and mutual-TLS transport
tasks.body: Deliverable: Ed25519 node identity persisting across restart, owner-only key file, and mutual TLS with peers authorized by key fingerprint (never hostname). Evidence: internal/identity/, commit `7011c77`; criteria C-ID-1..5, C-TR-1..9.

tasks.title: Replicated group log and signed group state (A-5)
tasks.body: Deliverable: append-only, hash-chained group log that only the epoch owner sequences; administrators act through signed proposals embedded by the owner; transport trust derived from the roster. Evidence: internal/grouplog/, internal/membership/, internal/replication/, commits `b310532`, `3af812f`, `84cf9af`, `4f90ee6`; criteria C-PO-9..23, C-TR-9.

tasks.title: Owner succession over the wire with signed attestations
tasks.body: Deliverable: owner-absence watch driven by heartbeats; eligible successor collects signed quorum attestations, claims, and opens a new epoch that fences the former owner. Evidence: internal/group/, commit `6e06149`; criteria C-PO-7, C-PO-14, C-PO-15, C-PO-24.

tasks.title: Enrollment by short code and QR code
tasks.body: Deliverable: node joins end to end by 29-char Crockford base32 short code or QR, redeeming at the inviter over a key-pinned connection, approved by an administrator, admitted by a signed owner-sequenced event, then downloads the log from genesis. Evidence: internal/enrollment/, internal/federation/, commit `6417dd9`; criterion C-EN-1..6.

tasks.title: Durable state layer on SQLite
tasks.body: Deliverable: embedded SQLite persistence with atomic transactions, owner-only files, indexed retention expiry, and fixed-width chronological timestamps; all stores survive restart. Evidence: internal/state (or equivalent), commits `1bed439`, `15069ff`, `d57e5c0`; criteria C-ST-1..11.

tasks.title: Encrypted backup and restore
tasks.body: Deliverable: AES-256-GCM backups of node key, certificate, and durable state under a PBKDF2 passphrase; tamper/wrong-passphrase refusal; restore never overwrites; restored owner held back until caught up. Evidence: internal/backup/, commit `dbe3500`; criteria C-ST-7, C-ST-10, C-ST-11.

tasks.title: Audit events with two layers of redaction
tasks.body: Deliverable: audit log with an allow-list for detail and registered-secret scrubbing on every field; enrollment, group log changes including equivocation, and block decisions audited without secrets. Evidence: internal/audit/, commit `c5e8a98`; criterion C-OP-1.

tasks.title: Daemon and CLI administration, container deployment
tasks.body: Deliverable: node runs as a containerized daemon administered from the CLI/admin API on loopback with an owner-only token; finds/joins at most one group; image builds and reports healthy. Evidence: cmd/jellymesh/, deploy/, Dockerfile, commits `b9b7c91`, `0c353e6`; criteria C-OP-5, C-OP-6; manual M-6.

tasks.title: Jellyfin source adapter as a non-administrator service user
tasks.body: Deliverable: read own Jellyfin as a dedicated non-admin service user; sees only granted libraries; paged item enumeration; ancestor-based library resolution; re-authenticates on token refusal; refuses administrator credentials/keys. Evidence: internal/ (adapter), commit `28a1ffb`; criteria C-SA-1, C-SA-2; manual M-7 confirmed against real Jellyfin 10.11.11 (commit `4071160`).

tasks.title: Source catalog: publication, revisions, tombstones, authorization
tasks.body: Deliverable: source catalog with incremental revisioned changes, confirmed tombstones with retention, and per-item authorization against the item's live library. Evidence: internal/catalog/, commit `a112359`; criteria C-CA-1, C-CA-2, C-CA-4.

tasks.title: Declared root paths and publication pause (A-9)
tasks.body: Deliverable: an operator declares each published library's root paths; every refresh checks item paths and pauses/withdraws the publication when an item falls outside. Evidence: internal/policy; criterion C-CA-3; assumption A-9.

tasks.title: Protected-library enforcement
tasks.body: Deliverable: a protected library (e.g. Cedar Family Movies) is absent from remote catalog, search, artwork, subtitles, and playback, including by guessed identifier, and is refused even if the service user can see it. Evidence: internal/policy; criterion C-PR-1.

tasks.title: Destination opt-out enforcement and catalog transport
tasks.body: Deliverable: catalogs flow between members over mutual TLS; destination drops opted-out items even if sent; source never sends them; blocked or non-member destinations get nothing. Evidence: internal/replication/catalog, commit `cebbb91`; criteria C-PR-2, C-CA-5, C-OP-7.

tasks.title: Wire the catalog into the daemon; drop the administrator API key
tasks.body: Deliverable: the daemon serves the catalog through its member routes using the non-admin service user instead of an administrator key. Evidence: commit `0dd6c60`; assumptions A-8.

tasks.title: Materialize remote catalogs into the generated root
tasks.body: Deliverable: generated .strm references, NFO metadata, subtitles, and posters written atomically; one folder per strong identity with one source-named file per source; no provider IDs in paths. Evidence: internal/materialize, commits `b0a1419`, `c30b4d7`; criteria C-MA-1..5, C-PR-3.

tasks.title: Local media relay with ranges, HEAD, and cancellation
tasks.body: Deliverable: destination relay serves media/subtitles/images from the source over mutual TLS, supports ranges, HEAD, cancellation and backpressure without full buffering, and authorizes locally (allow-listed clients, issued unrevoked references, destination policy per request). Evidence: internal/relay, commit `5790113`, `d3126fa`; criteria C-PB-1, C-PR-5.

tasks.title: Per-destination bandwidth ceiling and safe source-unavailable handling
tasks.body: Deliverable: a source enforces a per-destination bandwidth ceiling shared by all that destination's streams; an unavailable source fails cleanly (502) without destructive catalog pruning. Evidence: internal/limits, commit `d3126fa`; criteria C-PB-2, C-PB-3; assumption A-1 (ceiling half).

tasks.title: Source-side head cache for Jellyfin's repeated probes (C-PB-5)
tasks.body: Deliverable: the relay answers repeated PlaybackInfo probes from a bounded per-revision head cache, confirming each hit with a bodiless HEAD and stitching exactly past the head. Evidence: commit `24de056`, `82bf0da`; criterion C-PB-5.

tasks.title: Full playback chain on real Jellyfin 10.11.11 (M-9)
tasks.body: Deliverable: two Jellyfin containers and two Jellymesh nodes on one Docker network; walnut joined cedar's group by short code, materialized the film with subtitle, and streamed exact bytes through the relay. Evidence: lab/playcheck/run-throwaway.sh, commit `dc8c52f`; manual M-9, also M-8 (layout) and M-7 (adapter).

tasks.title: Compromise-recovery runbook
tasks.body: Deliverable: operator runbook for compromised node key; recovery is by re-enrollment (a fresh key is a distinct peer), not rotation. Evidence: docs/runbook-compromise-recovery.md, commit `46db94d`; criteria C-OP-2, C-OP-4.

tasks.title: Phase 4: identity, grouping, and progress
tasks.body: Deliverable: strong work identity and alternate versions, server labels and source metadata, local-only favourites/ratings/history, and validated client-specific version selection. Evidence for the gap: docs/design-spec.md section 16 Phase 4; conformance C-HI-6 PARTIAL (no episode addressing, plan-review D6).

children.title: Episode-level work identity (series+season+episode)
children.body: Current flat type/provider/id triple fails to restore most TV progress. plan-review D6; C-HI-6 PARTIAL.

children.title: Merge a remote version with a local copy via the Jellyfin merge API
children.body: A-4/A-11: merging remote with a local copy of the same film still needs POST /Videos/MergeVersions and is left to Phase 4.

children.title: Music scope decision and separate Friends Music library
children.body: Music is out of v1 (A-3); if it returns it must be contained in a separate library. Validate music behaviour per design-spec Phase 4.

children.title: Server labels and source metadata in generated artifacts
children.body: Version labels by source and richer source metadata; design-spec section 10.

tasks.title: Purge generated content without losing per-user history (C-HI-5)
tasks.body: What's left: the ledger and retention halves are proven, but the purge path that drives them does not exist yet. Evidence: docs/conformance.md C-HI-5 PARTIAL.

tasks.title: Source-side transcode for streams above the bandwidth ceiling (C-PB-4)
tasks.body: What's left: implement requesting a transcoded rendition from source Jellyfin when a requested media source exceeds the ceiling, instead of throttling/cloning. Evidence: docs/conformance.md C-PB-4 PENDING; assumption A-1 second half.

tasks.title: Public HTTPS from an external network without Tailscale (M-2/M-2a)
tasks.body: What's left: establish a reachable public address (guard against CGNAT in 100.64.0.0/10), then a domain, DNS, port forward, and certificate so federation works without Tailscale. Evidence: docs/conformance.md M-2, M-2a.

tasks.title: Backup, restore, and rollback drills including compromise recovery (M-3)
tasks.body: What's left: run the drills against the lab (C-ST-7/10/11 are in place); rehearse docs/runbook-compromise-recovery.md. Evidence: docs/conformance.md M-3.

tasks.title: Multi-home pilot surviving reboots, outages, renewal, library changes (M-4)
tasks.body: What's left: the genuine long pole — a second household running alpha software over weeks. Cannot be simulated. Evidence: docs/conformance.md M-4.

tasks.title: First join to a group of realistic size (M-5)
tasks.body: What's left: measure first-join item count against a real catalog size; throughput is known at 4.72 items/s (phase-0-results.md section 4). Evidence: docs/conformance.md M-5.

tasks.title: Client matrix: stock Jellyfin clients browse, play, seek, resume (M-1/M-1a)
tasks.body: What's left: no Jellyfin client has yet played a federated item; validate Web (available now against hand-authored .strm), Android, Android TV, iOS/Swiftfin, Roku. Evidence: docs/conformance.md M-1, M-1a — the largest untested assumption.

tasks.title: Phase 5 hardening, failure injection, and supported-version documentation
tasks.body: What's left: public HTTPS and failure-injection tests, the drills and pilot above, and documented supported Jellyfin versions and unsupported client behaviour. Evidence: docs/design-spec.md section 16 Phase 5, section 17 release gates.

tasks.title: Phase 6: stretch UX (heartbeat/offline detail, provider health, source avatar)
tasks.body: What's left: management-surface heartbeat and offline detail, provider-health rendering in Jellyfin Web, a client-independent source avatar convention, and exploring direct client-to-provider playback. Evidence: docs/design-spec.md section 16 Phase 6.

tasks.title: Direct peer connections: reachable addresses, hole-punched UDP media over QUIC (A-16)
tasks.body:
Every node advertises an address members can reach over TCP (router port forward, or Tailscale Funnel in raw-TCP mode). That address carries control traffic and arranges connections; media prefers a direct QUIC connection over a hole-punched UDP path, falling back to the advertised address when punching fails. No central matchmaker: the roster already holds every member's address.

Done when C-NT-1 to C-NT-6 are PASS and M-2 and M-12 have been performed.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Prototype: hole-punched QUIC transfer between two networks
children.body:
A throwaway lab tool (lab/punchcheck): each end learns its outside UDP address by STUN, the two exchange addresses over one side's advertised TCP address, punch, open QUIC, and time a transfer of a real film. Report punch success, time to connect, and sustained throughput, plus whether each NAT's mapping varies by destination.

Needs one end outside the home network (a laptop on a phone hotspot, or the pilot friend). Decides whether the design goes ahead unchanged.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Reachability requirement and join-time address check (C-NT-1)
children.body:
The approver's node dials the joiner's advertised address over mutual TLS and checks that the joiner's key answers there before signing the admission. Refuse clearly, naming the address, when it does not. Document the two accepted routes (port forward; Funnel raw TCP, never Funnel HTTPS).

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Cedar: advertise through Funnel raw TCP on port 10000 (M-2)
children.body:
Funnel allows only 443, 8443 and 10000; 443 is FiveyTools and 8443 is the tailnet-only Kaneo, so use 10000: `tailscale funnel --bg --tcp 10000 tcp://localhost:18443`. Widen the node's federation listener to reach it, set JELLYMESH_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME=cedar.sungrazer-shade.ts.net:10000, and verify from an outside network that the pinned-key TLS handshake survives the passthrough. Needs the user's go-ahead, since it exposes the node to the internet.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: STUN discovery on the QUIC socket and NAT-type detection (C-NT-2)
children.body:
Query public STUN servers (configurable list, e.g. Google and Cloudflare) on the same UDP socket the QUIC transport uses, multiplexing STUN with QUIC. Ask two servers to tell a destination-dependent mapping from an endpoint-independent one. Keep a fresh result and re-query on network change.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Signalling: authenticated direct-path offers (C-NT-3)
children.body:
Offer and answer messages carrying each side's candidates (the outside UDP address and LAN addresses), exchanged only over the mutually authenticated connection to the source's advertised address, bound to that pair, with a short expiry and a nonce. Refuse offers from non-members, for other pairs, or replayed late.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: QUIC transport with pinned node keys and hole punching (C-NT-4)
children.body:
Add quic-go. QUIC uses the node's existing certificate, and peers are verified by fingerprint exactly as on TCP. Both ends send punch packets to each other's candidates at once, with retries and a deadline, then the destination dials. Keep-alives hold NAT mappings; one connection per peer is reused. A mismatched key is refused.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Media over the direct path with every relay guarantee (C-NT-5)
children.body:
The destination's relay fetches from the source over HTTP/3 on the punched connection. Ranges, HEAD, cancellation, the per-destination ceiling (C-PB-3), the head cache and its HEAD confirmation (C-PB-5), and per-request authorization by the source must behave exactly as over TCP. Bind the existing relay tests to both transports.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Fallback to the advertised address and per-peer path reporting (C-NT-6)
children.body:
When punching fails or the direct path drops mid-stream, continue over the advertised TCP address without an error reaching Jellyfin, and retry the direct path later. `jellymesh status` shows each peer's path (direct UDP, LAN, or fallback) and the node's NAT type.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Automated NAT lab for punching and fallback tests
children.body:
Docker topologies with Linux NAT (iptables MASQUERADE) emulating endpoint-independent and destination-dependent routers, including double NAT, so C-NT-4 and C-NT-6 are proven by repeatable tests, not only by manual runs.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Security review of the UDP surface
children.body:
Review the new exposure: unauthenticated packets reaching the QUIC socket, STUN spoofing, punch traffic used for amplification, signalling floods, and resource limits per peer. Add rate limits and audit events for direct-path setup and failures, with redaction as in C-OP-1.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Real-world validation across two homes (M-12)
children.body:
cedar (via Funnel) and the pilot friend's node stream a film over a punched path; measure connect time and throughput; then force the fallback and confirm playback continues. Record results in conformance M-12.

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

children.title: Operator guide: making a node reachable
children.body:
Step-by-step setup for a router port forward (including double NAT) and for Tailscale Funnel raw TCP, how to check it from outside, and troubleshooting (carrier-grade NAT, hard NAT, Funnel's HTTPS mode being wrong).

Design: docs/design-spec.md section 8, "Reachability and direct media paths"; decision A-16 in docs/conformance.md (58da01e).

tasks.title: Pilot packet for a second household (M-4)
tasks.body: A self-contained setup packet the friend's agent can follow: what Jellymesh is, requirements (Docker, Jellyfin 10.11.x, a reachable address by port forward or Funnel raw TCP), getting the software (collaborator access or an image file, to decide), compose file and service user, publishing, joining with a code sent separately, verification, what to report back (never credentials), and teardown. Depends on the operator guide and the join-time address check. Relates to #40.

tasks.title: Later: automatic port mapping and third-member relays
tasks.body: Not in the first cut of A-16. (1) Open the advertised port automatically by UPnP, NAT-PMP or PCP on single-NAT homes (Google Wifi supports all three; a double NAT defeats it). (2) Relay signalling through a third member when neither node is reachable. (3) Opt-in media relaying through a third member when punching fails at both ends.
